question: What is being noticed?
description: The organization detects a condition, anomaly, weak signal, or emerging change that may require interpretation.
possible_degradation: Weak signals remain unseen, filtered out, or treated as background noise.
consequence: Emerging conditions remain outside organizational awareness.
provenance: Existing signal-to-decision mechanism; Nieleze research architecture

question: What is being missed?
description: A detected or potentially detectable signal is weakened, absorbed, normalized, obscured, or prevented from reaching relevant decision-makers.
possible_degradation: Signals are attenuated, normalized, fragmented, buried in routine processes, or prevented from entering the decision process.
consequence: Important conditions fail to influence subsequent recognition and decision processes.
provenance: Existing signal-to-decision mechanism; Nieleze research architecture

question: Has the significance of the signal been recognized?
description: The organization distinguishes between noticing the presence of a signal and recognizing its significance for action.
possible_degradation: A signal is detected but its meaning, urgency, relevance, or implications are not understood.
provenance: Existing signal-to-decision mechanism; Nieleze research architecture

question: What does the signal mean?
description: Interpretation is constrained when ambiguity, cognitive load, fragmented information, or competing explanations restrict the organization's ability to determine significance.
possible_degradation: Ambiguity, cognitive load, fragmentation, or competing interpretations constrain understanding.
consequence: Organizations cannot reliably determine what action is warranted.
provenance: Existing signal-to-decision mechanism; Nieleze research architecture

question: Can the organization construct a coherent interpretation?
description: Different organizational actors construct incomplete, inconsistent, or competing accounts of the same emerging condition.
possible_degradation: Actors hold incomplete, conflicting, or locally coherent interpretations without sufficient integration.
consequence: Shared understanding breaks down and coordinated action becomes more difficult.
provenance: Existing signal-to-decision mechanism; Nieleze research architecture

question: When does the signal become actionable?
description: The threshold at which an interpreted condition is escalated for formal attention or intervention changes as circumstances, norms, incentives, or perceived risk change.
possible_degradation: Escalation criteria drift upward, become inconsistent, or fail to keep pace with changing conditions.
consequence: Action is delayed even as risk increases.
provenance: Existing signal-to-decision mechanism; Nieleze research architecture

question: Can the organization deliberate adequately before acting?
description: The available decision process becomes compressed by time pressure, information overload, uncertainty, or escalating demands.
possible_degradation: Decision processes become narrower, delayed, overly simplified, or excessively dependent on reduced signals.
consequence: Decision quality and range of available responses diminish.
provenance: Existing signal-to-decision mechanism; Nieleze research architecture

question: How much time remains to intervene?
description: The organization assesses how much effective intervention time remains between recognition of a condition and loss of viable response options.
possible_degradation: Recognition or intervention occurs after the effective intervention window has materially narrowed.
consequence: Available intervention options diminish and become more costly or constrained.
provenance: Existing signal-to-decision mechanism; Nieleze research architecture

question: Will existing safeguards contain the condition?
description: Existing safeguards, controls, boundaries, or containment mechanisms are assessed for their ability to prevent local disturbances from propagating.
possible_degradation: Protective barriers weaken, interact unexpectedly, or fail to activate.
consequence: Local disturbances can become systemic failures.
provenance: Existing signal-to-decision mechanism; Nieleze research architecture

question: Can the system still recover?
description: The organization assesses whether sufficient structural and temporal capacity remains to contain consequences and restore viable operation.
possible_degradation: Recognition or intervention occurs after recoverability has materially degraded.
consequence: Failure becomes harder, slower, or more costly to contain.
provenance: Existing signal-to-decision mechanism; Nieleze research architecture

question: Does the organization convert experience into structural change?
description: Experience from detection, escalation, intervention, and recovery is converted into retained knowledge, altered practice, or structural adaptation.
possible_degradation: Lessons are not retained, translated, assigned, or incorporated into future practice.
consequence: The same structural vulnerabilities can recur.
provenance: Existing signal-to-decision mechanism; Nieleze research architecture
